detailed_description: The JSON to C# Converter generates simple C# class definitions from pasted JSON in the browser. You can edit the root class name, choose whether to output properties or fields, and toggle nullable handling for null values. The converter parses JSON with JSON.parse, uses the first item of an array when the input is an array of objects, creates nested classes for nested objects, infers basic types such as string, int, double, bool, List, object, and then lets you copy the generated code. It does not upload JSON files, analyze schemas, create XML documentation, use Roslyn, generate constructors or records, or provide syntax highlighting.
usage_steps: Paste JSON into the input textarea or edit the sample object.
Choose whether to generate properties or fields and whether null values should use nullable object output.
Click Convert to generate C# class code.
Review the output textarea and copy the generated code when needed.
usage_examples: Generate a starter C# class from a small API response sample.
Create nested classes from a pasted object that contains a child object.
Compare property and field output before copying a quick prototype.
Use the first object in a sample array to scaffold a basic C# class.
